title: The Herdsman's Dream of the Wolf

plan.english: A shepherd, Man-Minded, was dwelling in a village. He was guarding many sheep in the field. One night sleep seized him near the enclosure. Then he saw a dream. In sleep a great wolf came forth from the hill. It seized the ram and was carrying it away. Then Man-Minded woke up, trembling. He looked at the sheep; they were lying in the enclosure. He said: "Why am I afraid? The dream has deceived me." But he did not lie down; through the night he was sleepless. Early the wolf did arrive. But the shepherd was awake, and with the dogs he drove it away. So the dream rescued the ram. And he cherished the sheep, and he did not fear the night.

plan.english: A king was sitting, and he was sleepless. The earth was dry, and it did not rain. The cattle were thirsty. Then Sky, the father, put him to sleep and gave him a dream. In the dream a god was standing on a hill, and he spoke: "Give me a gift here! Then it shall rain for you." He woke up; the word was in his heart. He went up and gave him a cup and honey. Then it rained on three nights. They drank and became sated. And he praised Sky. And he became rich.

plan.english: Two brothers were guarding the cattle in the field. When it was getting dark, they lay down, and they were in sleep. In the night a stranger arrived and drove them away. When it grew bright, the brothers woke up. Of-Good-Fame said: "Brother, our cattle are gone!" Of-Divine-Race said: "Let us seek them." They tracked them to the water. There they caught sight of them and the stranger, lying in sleep. They drove them home. He did not wake up. Sleep seized the cattle, and sleep gave them back. They enclosed them; afterwards they were sleepless.

plan.english: The wife of a warrior was seeing a dream at night. A snake was lying in her own house. She became afraid, and she went to her who knows. She said: "Mother, in my sleep I saw a snake in my house. What does the dream say?" The Kindly One pointed it out: "Do not be afraid, daughter. The snake is the guardian of the household. A son will be born to you, and it will protect him." And he was born to her. The snake lay near the fire, and he grew up and was healthy. The wife gave the Kindly One a measure of flour.

plan.english: Two daughters were trembling at night. They said: "Mother, why does the night come? We are trembling." She answered: "Do not tremble, my dear ones. Night is the sister of Dawn. She clothes the earth, and the sheep lie in sleep. Then Dawn, the daughter of Sky, comes forth, and they wake up. She does not deceive; she protects those who sleep." Then they were lying down, and sleep took them.

plan.english: A warrior was lying by the fire. He was afraid; the hostile ones were many. Then sleep came upon him, and Perkʷunos stood over him in a dream. He was grasping a pointed tool in his hand. He spoke: "Warrior, why are you afraid? I slew the serpent; I shall protect you. Early stand up, and you will overpower them." He woke up, and he did not tremble. His heart grew strong. At dawn he stood up and overpowered the hostile ones. Great fame reached him, and he praised Perkʷunos.

title: The Long Sleep under the Hazel

plan.english: Of-Good-Horses went to the pasture and lay down under a hazel. A great sleep seized him. He lay in sleep through many nights. The leaves fell, and the leaves grew again. Then he woke up and went home. In the house a man was standing. Of-Good-Horses did not know him, and he said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am the son of Of-Good-Horses. My father went away and vanished." Then he was astonished, and he said: "Son, I am your father!" He became joyful, and he seated him by the fire. He said: "You are grown, and I was in sleep."

title: The Guest Who Came by Night

plan.english: A woman was in sleep. In the night she heard someone. She woke up and caught sight of a stranger sitting by the fire. She trembled and said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am hungry and thirsty." She gave him fish and honey, and he ate and drank. Then he said: "Woman, you are good. May the gods give you good things." She lay down again, and sleep took her. Early he vanished. But there stood a cup, and it was becoming full of honey. The guest was a god. She was sipping from it, and the honey became tasty.

plan.english: Much-Famed was seeing in a dream his own house burning. The fire was licking it. He woke up and was sweating. At dawn he went to her who knows. He told her the dream. And the fame of Much-Famed grew. They were singing his name.

title: The Dog That Did Not Sleep

plan.english: A shepherd had a dog. At night he was in sleep, but the dog was sleepless. It was listening, and it heard well. A wolf was coming, creeping toward the sheep. It cried out and ran at it. The shepherd woke up and seized a pointed tool. The wolf fled away. He said to it: "Dear dog, you are my guardian. When I sleep, you are awake." He gave it grease and fish, and the dog licked his hand.

title: The Boy Who Wanted to See the Night

plan.english: A king's son, Of-Good-Race, wanted to see the night. His mother said: "Lie down!" But he did not lie down; he sat on the hill. He looked at the sky; it was turning. A beast crept past; Of-Good-Race trembled, but he did not flee. Then it became bright, and the sun came forth. He came down, and he said: "I have seen the night and the dawn. It was great, but she was dear." Then sleep seized him.

It became bright, and the men woke up. The shepherds drove the cattle to the pastures. The wives milked them. The men were working, and they were pulling the harrow. They sang and praised Dawn: "Daughter of Sky, come to us again!"

plan.english: The father of Fame-from-the-Gods had died. One night Fame-from-the-Gods was seeing him in a dream. He was sitting in a boat. He said: "Son, I am thirsty. Remember me! Give me poured water and honey!" The boat was leaving, and Fame-from-the-Gods woke up. His heart was trembling in fear. Early he went out and gave him poured honey. He came in a dream, and he said: "I have drunk; I am satisfied." Then he did not come again. Now Fame-from-the-Gods remembers him at the feast.

plan.english: Sleep is the brother of Death. By night Sleep comes to men. He grasps them, and early he lets them go. Death seizes them and does not let them go. When it grew bright, Of-Many-Horses woke up and went away. Death went away, but she will come again. He is the giver of good things. Men, praise him: he lets you go!

plan.english: Of-Many-Horses had swift horses. In the night a stranger was stealing a horse from the enclosure. Of-Many-Horses was in sleep, and in a dream he was seeing that. He woke up and went to the enclosure, but he did not find the horse. Through the night he tracked him. Early he caught sight of him. He was drinking, and the horse was eating leaves. Of-Many-Horses cried out: "Stranger, you were stealing my horse!" He became afraid, and he fled into the water and swam away. And he led his own horse home. He was smearing it with grease.

He went, and Of-Good-Mind said to him: "A beast is lying in your heart: it is trembling. Give a gift to the Night, and the beast will flee." At night he put wool and honey on the hill. He made a pledge to her, and then sleep came to him. When it grew bright, he woke up and became joyful.

There she found him, and she was lifting him up. He had gone astray, and he was thirsty. She gave it to him, and he drank and lived. He said: "Sister, how did you know?" She said: "The dream led me." Now he cherishes his sister.

He gave her a ram and wool. He was loaded with fame.

He trembled: "The hostile ones will steal them!" He sought them on the hill and by the water. His dog was following him. The dog tracked the sheep and found them. Kindly drove them into the enclosure. He said: "I shall not sleep under the hazel again."

I caught sight of a wolf, and I killed it. The wolf died; I did not die."

He woke up; he yoked the horses and drove against them. But the hostile ones were many, and they overpowered him. He fled and said: "He deceived me with a dream." Men, do not follow dreams!

But they were afraid of it, and they did not come up. He was sleepless; he sang to the Fire: "Fire, protect me, and burn!" It burned; it became bright, and they went away. He went down, and he arrived. His trembling became slack.

He said: "A dream gives water, but the thirsty one does not drink it." He stood up and went out, and he drank. Then he lay down again, and the dream did not come.

And he gave him a reward, a horse.

plan.english: A king was holding Of-Goodly-Fame in an enclosure. A guardian was watching him by night. Of-Goodly-Fame chanted to Perkʷunos: "Perkʷunos, free me!" The king was angry, but the guardian said: "A god put me to sleep. No one has power against a god." Then the king let him go.

Then he woke up, and he was hungry again. He said: "The dream was nourishing me, but my gut did not become full." Then he went to the water and seized a fish with a net. He cooked it and ate it up, and he was sated.

plan.english: Of-Good-Speech was ploughing a field. He became tired and lay down, and the Night put him to sleep. He woke up: the apples were red, and they were ripening. The yoke had broken, and his own cattle had gone astray. He was going to the village, and they did not recognize him. They said: "Who is this?" His wife came forth, and she knew him. She said: "Husband, where were you? Twice the apples have ripened!" He was astonished: "Great is sleep!"

He was going to the village, and they did not recognize him.
They said: "Who is this?"
His wife came forth, and she knew him.
She said: "Husband, where were you?
Twice the apples have ripened!"
He was astonished: "Great is sleep!"

plan.english: The herdsman Of-Goodly-Fame saw a wolf in a dream. It ate up his cattle. He went to her who knows and told her the dream. She said: "The wolf is hunger; hunger will come. Put flour inside!" He put the flour inside. Then the earth dried up, and hunger arrived in the village. The people were hungry, but Of-Goodly-Fame gave them flour. His fame became great.

title: Where the Sun Goes at Night

plan.english: A boy, Of-Good-Speech, said: "Father, where does the sun go at night?" He was pointing: "It sinks under the earth. There the wheel of the sun turns through the night." "Does it sleep there?" "It does not sleep. It goes, and early it comes forth again. Men lie in sleep, but the sun is alert. Sky keeps looking at us." Then he lay down, and he was not afraid. Now he wants to see the wheel of the sun.

clauses.english: A boy, Of-Good-Speech, said: "Father, where does the sun go at night?"

"It does not sleep.
It goes, and early it comes forth again.
Men lie in sleep, but the sun is alert.
Sky keeps looking at us."
Then he lay down, and he was not afraid.
Now he wants to see the wheel of the sun.

plan.english: A beast was coming to the village, and it was devouring the sheep. The men were trembling, and no one went out. Then the warrior Of-Divine-Race said: "I shall not sleep this night." He sat by the sheep with a net, and he was awake. In the night the beast came creeping. He threw the net over it and struck it down. When it grew bright, the men caught sight of the beast, and they praised the warrior: "You were sleepless, and now we sleep." They were flaying it.

title: The Shepherd's Tale by the Fire

plan.english: By the fire a shepherd was telling a tale to the guests. He said: "Hear my tale! My father was guarding horses in the field. One night a god came to him in a dream, and he said: 'Shepherd, the horses will flee; guard them!' He woke up, and he stood by them through the night. The sky rumbled, and the horses trembled. But he held them, and they did not flee. When it grew bright, he praised him." They were listening, and they were sleepless.

clauses.english: By the fire a shepherd was telling a tale to the guests.
He said: "Hear my tale!
My father was guarding horses in the field.
One night a god came to him in a dream, and he said:

He woke up, and he stood by them through the night.
The sky rumbled, and the horses trembled.
But he held them, and they did not flee.
When it grew bright, he praised him."
They were listening, and they were sleepless.

plan.english: Of-Good-Fame was making ready a boat. At night he was seeing in a dream the boat sinking. He went to Of-Good-Mind and told her. She said: "Do not go on the water! It will swallow the boat." He sat down. Men took his boat and went out on it. Perkʷunos roared, and the boat sank. They swam, and they came forth. Of-Good-Fame praised the woman: "Your word rescued me." They brought her a gift.

Men took his boat and went out on it.
Perkʷunos roared, and the boat sank.
They swam, and they came forth.
Of-Good-Fame praised the woman: "Your word rescued me."
They brought her a gift.

plan.english: Of-Goodly-Fame was going through the night, and he became cold. He caught sight of a fire, and near it he saw a house. Of-Good-Gifts came forth from it and said: "Guest, enter, and sit down here!" She clothed him with wool, and she gave him honey; he ate and became warm. Then she laid him down, and he was in sleep. Early he woke up: he was lying on a hill. The house had vanished, and the fire had become cold. But his heart was warm, and he was not hungry. He said: "Was this a dream, or the house of a god?" Then he was going on the way.

plan.english: A father and his son, Of-Good-Race, were guarding the horses at night. He said: "Son, I have become tired. Watch them; I shall lie down." Of-Good-Race said: "Lie down, father; I am alert." The father was lying down in sleep; Of-Good-Race sat and looked at the horses. But sleep was creeping toward him. He stood up and walked around the horses, and he sang. At dawn he woke up: "Of-Good-Race, did you sleep?" "I did not sleep; I walked and I sang, and the horses are here." And he cherished him.

title: How the Wise Woman Came to Know

plan.english: Of-Good-Mind lay on the hill on three nights. She did not eat, and she did not drink. Then Sky caused her to see the course of the sun. She saw the dreams of men. She came down, and now she knows dreams. They come to her and tell dreams. She speaks, and they hear her. Whom the gods cause to see, that one knows. Her name is famous.

plan.english: A dog was lying by the enclosure. In sleep it was crying out and trembling. A girl said: "Father, what does the dog see?" He said: "It sees a beast in the field. There it is running and seizing the beast. Whoever sleeps, that one sees dreams." Then the dog woke up and stood up. It looked around, and it was seeking it. She gave it grease, and it sat down.
